outcome: Prevalence of proximate umbilical cord insertions (PCI)
cohort: The study included 369 monochorionic (MC) placentas that had not been treated with laser surgery.
finding: The study defined proximate umbilical cord insertions (PCI) as a distance below the 5th centile, approximately 4 cm throughout gestation, finding that PCI are common in MC monoamniotic placentas and associated with higher rates of superficial arterio-arterial and/or veno-venous anastomoses.
cross-section timing: The study retrospectively analyzed placentas collected during an unspecified study period.
gest_age: Gestational age (weeks) was used to establish the reference range for the distance between cord insertions.
